title: Bhooth Bangla Just Crossed ₹267 Crore Worldwide. In Its Seventh Week. Akshay Kumar Has Not Had a Run Like This in Years.
excerpt: Priyadarshan's horror-comedy has earned ₹180 crore net in India and is now chasing Akshay's own Housefull 5 record — a milestone that seemed unthinkable when the film quietly opened 47 days ago.
body:
Forty-seven days into its theatrical run, Bhooth Bangla refuses to leave the building.

Akshay Kumar and Priyadarshan's horror-comedy has now crossed ₹267 crore worldwide gross, with India net collections standing at ₹180.45 crore after its seventh Tuesday. The film continues to play in over 1,500 shows daily across India, and its BookMyShow ticket sales have surpassed 33.75 lakh — numbers that would be impressive for a film in its second week, let alone its seventh.

On Day 47, the film earned ₹0.60 crore net in India, a 20 percent jump over Monday's ₹0.50 crore. A midweek bump at this stage of a theatrical run is uncommon enough to be noteworthy. When the film in question is a mid-budget horror-comedy directed by a 68-year-old filmmaker, it becomes something closer to remarkable.

## The Housefull 5 Race

The number that matters most right now is ₹183.38 crore. That is the lifetime India net collection of Housefull 5, currently Akshay Kumar's highest-grossing post-COVID release. Bhooth Bangla sits at ₹180.45 crore — a gap of just ₹2.93 crore.

At the current pace of ₹50–60 lakh per weekday with weekend jumps, trade analysts expect Bhooth Bangla to surpass the Housefull 5 record within the next 8 to 10 days, likely before its eighth week concludes. If it does, it will become the most successful solo Akshay Kumar release since the pandemic reshaped theatrical economics, and only the second film in his post-2020 career to cross the ₹185 crore net mark in India.

The overseas numbers tell their own story. With a gross of ₹53.75 crore from international markets, Bhooth Bangla has demonstrated that NRI audiences are still willing to turn up for a well-made Indian comedy. The film's total domestic gross stands at ₹213.74 crore, making the ₹267 crore worldwide figure a combination of sustained Indian performance and steady overseas contribution.

## Why This Film Worked

The Akshay Kumar career narrative of the last three years has been dominated by underperformance. From Samrat Prithviraj to Selfiee, from Bade Miyan Chote Miyan to Khel Khel Mein, the actor has released film after film that failed to connect with audiences. The criticism became a loop: Akshay was doing too many films, choosing the wrong scripts, phoning in performances, losing touch with what audiences wanted.

Bhooth Bangla broke that loop. It did so not by reinventing Akshay Kumar, but by putting him back in the hands of the man who understood his strengths best. Priyadarshan, the Malayalam filmmaker who directed Hera Pheri, Bhool Bhulaiyaa, Garam Masala, and Hungama, has always known how to extract comedy from Kumar — not through dialogue but through reaction, timing, and the careful construction of absurd situations.

The horror-comedy genre gave them a playground. Indian audiences have shown, through Stree, Bhediya, and Munjya, that they have an appetite for films that mix supernatural premises with genuine laughs. Bhooth Bangla leaned into that appetite with a Priyadarshan touch — slower, more character-driven, less reliant on VFX spectacle and more dependent on ensemble chemistry.

## The Multiplex Hold

What makes the seventh-week performance particularly striking is the multiplex data. On Day 47, the three major national chains — PVR, INOX, and Cinepolis — recorded a combined 27,000 ticket sales across roughly 550 shows, maintaining an overall occupancy of 26 percent. PVR led with 12,580 tickets at 28.6 percent occupancy, followed by INOX at 10,890 tickets and Cinepolis at the same figure with 21.9 percent occupancy.

These are not blockbuster numbers. But they are steady, reliable, and profitable. The film has already screened nearly 240,000 shows across its run — a staggering figure that reflects both distributor confidence and genuine audience demand. In an industry where most films disappear from multiplexes after two weeks, Bhooth Bangla's persistence is its own kind of statement.

## The NRI Angle

For the Indian diaspora, Bhooth Bangla carries a specific kind of nostalgia. Priyadarshan's comedies were formative experiences for NRI families in the early 2000s — Hera Pheri and Hungama were the films you watched when relatives visited, the films that played on repeat during Diwali weekends, the films that proved Bollywood could be genuinely, universally funny without needing subtitles for the punchlines.

Bhooth Bangla is still screening in select theatres across the US and UK. For NRIs who have been waiting for the right Akshay Kumar film to show up at their local AMC or Cinepolis, this is the one. After 47 days, it is still there. After ₹267 crore, it is still growing. And after years of diminishing returns, Akshay Kumar has finally found his way back to an audience that was always willing to laugh — they just needed the right film to show up.

The king of the comedy-action double bill and the master of the Malayalam remake have proven, one more time, that the old formula still works. You just have to execute it properly.
author: Diaspora Desk
